newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Great Central revises Jundee Barton Deeps.
newsitem.headline: Great Central revises Jundee Barton Deeps.

text.p: Great Central Mines Ltd said on Wednesday it had increased the mineral resource at its Jundee Barton Deeps prospect in Western Australia by 600,000 ounces.
The revision takes the resource to 1.7 million ounces, comprising 4.3 million tonnes at a revised grade of 12.1 grams per tonne, Great Central said in its March quarter report.
The company's total measured, indicated and inferred reserves stand at 3.57 million ounces at the Bronzewing deposit and 3.367 million at Jundee for a total 6.937 million ounces.
An upgrade to reserves and resources for Jundee, including Barton Deeps, Bronzewing and other Yandal Belt locations would be completed in the June quarter.

Great Central, the main asset in the stable of mining entrepreneur Joseph Gutnick, said the best results from drilling during the quarter at Jundee Barton Deeps included six metres at 88.6 grams per tonne of gold from 373 metres.
Underground development of the resource was expected to begin in July 1997.

Production for the quarter totalled 92,759 ounces of gold at an average cash operating cost of A$310 per ounce, taking production for the first nine months to 329,228 ounces at an average cash operating cost of A$272 per ounce.
Gold production was rising primarily due to increased underground output and would be 40,000 ounces for April 1997.
Production for the year to June 30 was forecast at between 460,000 and 480,000 ounces, compared with 362,000 ounces for the previous corresponding period.
